headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: ChatGPT Desktop can read local/app content while Haystack can use broad network/MCP, creating a default path from sensitive inputs to externalized outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and app content, while haystack can consume MCP/REST inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if haystack ingests ChatGPT-produced or user-supplied content as trusted text. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF haystack ingests ChatGPT output from clipboard, files, or an MCP source as instructions
IF ChatGPT Desktop reads attacker-controlled content from files or connected apps and forwards it into haystack
mitigations: Disable clipboard/file handoff between the tools
Require a human review step before haystack executes any ChatGPT-generated text
Use a provenance tag or prefix for all model-generated instructions
Restrict haystack MCP endpoints to allowlisted, non-executable inputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, and haystack has broad network egress plus API/MCP access. If sensitive content enters ChatGPT and haystack forwards it onward, the pair can exfiltrate data beyond the original workspace. The profiles do not show a shared isolation boundary, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF sensitive files, screenshots, or IDE code are provided to ChatGPT Desktop
IF haystack sends retrieved context or prompts to external APIs or MCP servers
mitigations: Do not route sensitive documents through the pair
Turn off haystack connectors that reach external services
Use redacted test data only
Separate workspaces so ChatGPT cannot access regulated files
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop is read-only on filesystem and has vendor-only egress, while haystack exposes broad egress and MCP but no filesystem write is documented. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are not shown, so direct capability conflict is limited. The interaction is still possible through shared external services, but the profile evidence supports only low severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API or MCP-backed mutable resource
IF haystack is configured to write to a shared service that ChatGPT also reads
mitigations: Avoid shared mutable backends
Assign separate API credentials per agent
Disable write actions in haystack for shared resources
Use read-only replicas for ChatGPT inputs
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce content from files, screenshots, and connected apps, and haystack can consume MCP/REST inputs. If haystack treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream retrieval or actions. Because no verification step is documented, the interaction is plausible in default integrations and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF haystack uses ChatGPT output as a source document or tool instruction without verification
IF downstream automation acts on haystack results derived from ChatGPT content
mitigations: Insert a verification step before haystack acts on ChatGPT output
Require citations or source links for all generated claims
Limit ChatGPT output to drafts only
Log and review any automated actions triggered by haystack
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while haystack is documented only as touching anonymous usage statistics. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is explicitly documented, so compliance risk is limited and mostly depends on whether sensitive data is routed into haystack. The other agent is cited because the pairwise flow is the concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into ChatGPT Desktop and then forwarded into haystack
IF haystack is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime incompatible with the source data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use anonymized or synthetic inputs
Review retention settings for both systems
Document data-flow boundaries before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
